description:
Turn the positive 19513245 consumer evidence into a reviewed library-layer design before any production implementation ships.

## Background

The completed byte-field assessment confirms consumer benefit for
`FieldVec::axpy` and dense `FieldMatrix` product, while attributing a large part
of the current cost to repeated table construction and per-element dispatch.
It does not confirm `FieldMatrix::matvec`, and it does not justify a public byte
region API or byte-packed storage redesign.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Publish and link a reviewed design for a byte product table cached per field or compile-time field configuration, plus canonical `FieldVec` and `FieldMatrix` hooks for the confirmed axpy and dense-product consumers.
- [hard] REQ-02: Preserve the representations callers already hold, the one canonical dispatch abstraction, a tested scalar fallback, and existing overlap and allocation contracts; the design introduces no public byte-region API or storage redesign.
- [hard] REQ-03: Specify conformance for every byte coefficient, zero and one, unaligned inputs, tails, both 0x11B and 0x11D polynomials, cache lifetime and thread safety; production unsafe code remains isolated to the kernel crates.
- [hard] REQ-04: Create reviewed worker-sized JIT implementation and confirmation scope before shipping, pinned to the 19513245 profile and confirmation receipts. `FieldMatrix::matvec` remains excluded until a separate paired consumer campaign confirms it.

## Notes

The source decision and measurements are linked from `@/issue/19513245`.
